summary: Right-handed volleyball spike in the air, bow-and-arrow arm cock: hitting elbow high and back, non-hitting arm pointing at the ball, back arched.

roles.l_arm: non-hitting arm, pointing at the ball

environment.text: Net: top tape 2.43 m high, {fwd:net_top:pelvis} cm in front of the hips; the ball is still above and in front of the attacker.

cameras.name: side_low
cameras.text: Sharp focus on the cocked hitting arm and the arched back.

cameras.name: front_three_quarter
cameras.text: Both arms separated clearly: one pointing up at the ball, one drawn back like a bowstring.

cameras.name: wide_cinema
cameras.text: Wide frame from behind the attacker looking at the net and the blockers.

rules.why: hitting shoulder externally rotated on the way to maximum external rotation (160-180 deg in spikes)
hitting upper arm abducted about 90-120 deg, elbow at or above shoulder height
hitting elbow bent about 90 deg, hand near the ear
non-hitting arm raised toward the ball
upper back arched before the swing

text.action: a volleyball attacker in the air drawing the hitting arm back in a bow-and-arrow position before the spike
text.core: Airborne, feet {lowest_z} m above the floor, knees bent with the shins trailing behind; back arched and hitting shoulder rotated back; right elbow high at shoulder height and bent about 90 degrees, hand beside the ear; left arm straight, pointing up at the ball; chest open toward the ball.
text.gaze: Eyes on the ball above and in front.
cues: non-hitting arm leads and points at the ball
hitting shoulder rotated back for trunk rotation
hitting elbow high, hand at ear height
kinetic: body at the top of the jump, hair and jersey floating
slight motion blur on the hitting hand as it cocks back
chalk-white arena light rim-lighting the arched back
avoid: arm bent backwards at the elbow

sources.cite: Reeser et al. 2010, Sports Health: maximum external rotation 160-172 deg in spikes and jump serves (search extract)
Technique descriptions of the bow-and-arrow arm swing, summarised in Giatsis et al. 2022, JSSM
FIVB Coaches Manual Level II: left arm leads, right shoulder rotates back
Fuchs et al. 2019, J Sports Sci: elite jump heights 0.37-0.64 m
